concepts.def: A fluid is a substance that can flow. A fluid can be either a liquid or a gas, so gases as well as liquids exert pressure on the surfaces they are in contact with.

The pressure in fluids causes a force normal (at right angles) to any surface. This is true whichever way the surface faces: the force on the side wall of a tank is horizontal, the force on its base is vertical, and the force on a sloping surface is at right angles to that slope.
Pressure is the force acting normal to a surface divided by the area of that surface. For a fixed force, a smaller area gives a greater pressure, and a larger area gives a smaller pressure.

concepts.term: pressure = (force normal to a surface)/(area of that surface), p = F/A
concepts.def: The pressure at the surface of a fluid is calculated from pressure = (force normal to a surface)/(area of that surface), written p = F/A, with pressure p in pascals (Pa), force F in newtons (N) and area A in metres squared (m²). This is one of the equations you are expected to recall and apply.
The pascal is the unit of pressure. A pressure of 1 Pa is produced by a force of 1 N acting normal to an area of 1 m², so 1 Pa is 1 N/m².
F is the force acting normal to the surface, measured in newtons, N. Only the force at right angles to the surface is used; a force acting along the surface does not contribute to the pressure on it.
A is the area of the surface the force acts on, measured in metres squared, m². An area given in cm² must be converted before use: 1 m² = 10 000 cm², so divide an area in cm² by 10 000 to get m².

concepts.term: pressure = height of the column × density of the liquid × gravitational field strength, p = h ρ g
concepts.def: The pressure due to a column of liquid is calculated from pressure = height of the column × density of the liquid × gravitational field strength, written p = h ρ g, with p in pascals (Pa), h in metres (m), ρ in kilograms per metre cubed (kg/m³) and g in newtons per kilogram (N/kg). This equation is provided in the exam, so the skill being tested is selecting it and substituting into it correctly.

h is the vertical height of the column of liquid above the point being considered, measured in metres, m. It is the depth of that point below the liquid surface. It is not the width of the container, the total volume of liquid, or the height measured up from the base.
ρ is the density of the liquid in kilograms per metre cubed, kg/m³. Densities quoted in g/cm³ must be converted before use: 1 g/cm³ = 1000 kg/m³, so water of density 1.0 g/cm³ is 1000 kg/m³.

g is the gravitational field strength in newtons per kilogram, N/kg. It is not a force, and it is not measured in newtons. In any calculation the value of g will be given in the question, so use the value stated there.

concepts.term: Why pressure increases with height of column and with density
concepts.def: The pressure at a point in a liquid is caused by the weight of the liquid above that point. A taller column of liquid above the point means more liquid, and so a greater weight pressing down; a denser liquid has more mass in the same volume, and so also a greater weight above the point. Either change increases the pressure at that point, which is why p = h ρ g has both h and ρ as factors.

concepts.term: Difference in pressure between two depths
concepts.def: Because p = h ρ g, the difference in pressure between two depths in the same liquid depends on the difference in the height of liquid above them: difference in pressure = difference in height × density × gravitational field strength. The answer is in pascals, Pa.

A partially (or totally) submerged object experiences a greater pressure on the bottom surface than on the top surface, because the bottom surface is deeper and so has a taller column of liquid above it. The force on the bottom surface is therefore larger than the force on the top surface, creating a resultant force upwards. This force is called the upthrust.

Whether an object floats or sinks depends on the size of the upthrust compared with the object's weight. An object floats when the upthrust is equal to its weight. An object with a density less than the density of the liquid floats, coming to rest partly submerged; an object with a density greater than the density of the liquid sinks, because even when fully submerged the upthrust is smaller than its weight. It is the comparison of the two densities that matters, not the object's size or weight on its own.

The atmosphere is a thin layer of air round the Earth — thin relative to the size of the Earth. The atmosphere gets less dense with increasing altitude, so there is no sharp upper edge; the air simply thins out.

Air molecules colliding with a surface create atmospheric pressure. Each collision gives the surface a tiny force normal to it, and the huge number of collisions every second adds up to a steady pressure on every surface exposed to the air, in every direction.

concepts.term: Why atmospheric pressure decreases with height
concepts.def: The number of air molecules (and so the weight of air) above a surface decreases as the height of the surface above ground level increases. As height increases there is always less air above a surface than there is at a lower height, so atmospheric pressure decreases with an increase in height.

mcqs.q: In physics, what does the word 'fluid' mean?
options: A fluid must be a liquid, never a gas.
A fluid is anything that can be poured.
A fluid must be a gas, never a liquid.
A fluid can be either a liquid or a gas.
mcqs.explain: This is the definition given in the specification: both liquids and gases can flow and both exert pressure on surfaces.

mcqs.q: A gas is sealed inside a container. In which direction does the pressure of the gas exert a force on the container walls?
options: Downwards on every part of the container.
Sideways along each wall surface.
Outwards from the centre, at any angle.
At right angles to each wall surface.
mcqs.explain: The pressure in fluids causes a force normal (at right angles) to any surface, whichever way that surface faces.

mcqs.q: A crate rests on the floor. It exerts a force of 300 N normal to the floor over a contact area of 0.25 m². What pressure does the crate exert on the floor?
options: 75 Pa
mcqs.explain: p = F/A = 300 ÷ 0.25 = 1200 Pa, with force in newtons and area in metres squared.

mcqs.q: A pressure of 400 Pa acts normal to a surface of area 0.20 m². What is the size of the force acting normal to that surface?
options: 80 Pa
mcqs.explain: Rearranging p = F/A gives F = p A = 400 × 0.20 = 80 N.

mcqs.q: Which units must be used in p = F/A so that the pressure comes out in pascals?
options: F in newtons and A in centimetres squared
F in kilograms and A in metres squared
F in newtons and A in metres squared
F in newtons and A in metres cubed
mcqs.explain: The specification gives force, F, in newtons, N, and area, A, in metres squared, m², which together give pressure in pascals, Pa.

mcqs.q: A drawing pin is pushed into a board. The force on its flat head and the force at its sharp point are the same size. Which statement is correct?
options: The pressure at the point is smaller, because the contact area is smaller.
The pressure is the same at both, because the same force acts at both ends.
The pressure at the point is greater, because the area there is smaller.
The pressure is the same at both, because pressure depends on the material.
mcqs.explain: The same force divided by a much smaller area gives a much greater pressure, which is why the point penetrates the board.

mcqs.q: A force of 60 N acts normal to a surface of area 20 cm². What is the pressure on that surface?
options: 3 Pa
300 Pa

mcqs.q: Which statement best describes the Earth's atmosphere?
options: A thick layer of air with the same density at all heights.
A thin layer of air that gets less dense with height.
A thin layer of air that gets more dense with altitude.
A deep layer of air, far thicker than the Earth is wide.
mcqs.explain: The atmosphere is a thin layer relative to the size of the Earth, and it gets less dense with increasing altitude.

mcqs.q: Why does atmospheric pressure decrease as the height above the ground increases?
options: There is less air above the surface, so less weight of air presses on it.
Gravity is much weaker high up, so the air presses on the surface less.
The air is colder high up, so its molecules press on surfaces less hard.
There is less oxygen high up, and oxygen is what creates the pressure.
mcqs.explain: As height increases there is always less air above a surface than at a lower height, so fewer molecules and less weight of air press on it.

mcqs.q: What creates atmospheric pressure on a surface?
options: Air molecules pushing each other sideways.
The wind blowing over the surface.
Gravity pulling down on the surface itself.
Air molecules colliding with the surface.
mcqs.explain: Air molecules colliding with a surface create atmospheric pressure, each collision giving a small force normal to the surface.

mcqs.q: A weather balloon rises from ground level high into the atmosphere. What happens to the air outside the balloon as it rises?
options: The density stays the same and the atmospheric pressure falls.
The density falls but the atmospheric pressure stays the same.
The density falls and the atmospheric pressure falls as well.
The density rises and the atmospheric pressure rises as well.
mcqs.explain: The atmosphere gets less dense with increasing altitude, and with less air above, atmospheric pressure decreases with height.

mcqs.q: A diver is 12 m below the surface of water of density 1000 kg/m³. In this question use g = 9.8 N/kg. What is the pressure due to the water at that depth?
Which set of units must be used in p = h ρ g to give the pressure in pascals?
options: h in m, ρ in g/cm³, g in N/kg
h in m, ρ in kg/m³, g in N
h in m, ρ in kg/m³, g in N/kg
h in cm, ρ in kg/m³, g in N/kg
mcqs.explain: The specification gives the height of the column in metres, the density in kilograms per metre cubed and the gravitational field strength in newtons per kilogram.

mcqs.q: A tank contains oil of density 900 kg/m³ to a depth of 2.5 m. In this question use g = 9.8 N/kg. What is the pressure due to the oil at the base of the tank?
mcqs.explain: p = h ρ g = 2.5 × 900 × 9.8 = 22 050 Pa, using the value of g given in the question.

mcqs.q: Why is the pressure at a point in a liquid greater when there is a taller column of liquid above that point?
options: The liquid at the bottom is squashed into a smaller space.
There is a greater weight of liquid pressing down on that point.
Deeper liquid always has a greater density than shallow liquid.
The liquid above has further to fall before it reaches the point.
mcqs.explain: A taller column contains more liquid above the point, so a greater weight acts on it and the pressure is greater.

mcqs.q: A diver swims from a depth of 4.0 m to a depth of 10.0 m in water of density 1000 kg/m³. In this question use g = 9.8 N/kg. By how much does the pressure due to the water increase?
mcqs.explain: The difference in height is 10.0 − 4.0 = 6.0 m, so the increase in pressure is 6.0 × 1000 × 9.8 = 58 800 Pa.

mcqs.q: Why does a totally submerged object experience an upthrust?
options: The liquid underneath pushes up on it and nothing pushes down on it.
Liquid pressure acts upwards only, so anything in a liquid is pushed up.
The pressure on its bottom surface is greater than on its top surface.
The object's weight becomes smaller when it is put into the liquid.
mcqs.explain: The bottom surface is deeper, so the upward force on it exceeds the downward force on the top surface, giving a resultant force upwards called the upthrust.

mcqs.q: A solid object is placed in a liquid. Under what condition does the object float?
options: When the object is light, whatever the liquid it is placed in.
When the upthrust on the object is greater than its weight.
When the object's density is less than 1000 kg/m³, always.
When the object's density is less than the liquid's density.
mcqs.explain: An object less dense than the liquid comes to rest partially submerged, with the upthrust equal to its weight.

mcqs.q: The pressure due to a column of water is 4900 Pa. The water has a density of 1000 kg/m³ and g = 9.8 N/kg. What is the height of the column?
mcqs.explain: Rearranging p = h ρ g gives h = p/(ρ g) = 4900 ÷ (1000 × 9.8) = 0.50 m.

mcqs.q: Two open tanks are filled with water to the same depth. Tank Y is four times as wide as tank X. How does the pressure due to the water at the base of the tanks compare?
options: Greater in tank Y, because tank Y contains four times as much water.
Greater in tank X, because the base of tank X has a much smaller area.
Greater in tank X, because a narrow tank squashes the water together.
The same in both, because the water is at the same depth in each.
mcqs.explain: p = h ρ g contains no term for width or volume, so equal depths of the same liquid give equal pressures.

mcqs.q: A cube is held completely under water. Its top face is 0.10 m below the surface and its bottom face is 0.30 m below. The water has a density of 1000 kg/m³ and g = 9.8 N/kg. What is the difference in pressure between the bottom face and the top face?
options: 980 Pa
mcqs.explain: The difference in height is 0.30 − 0.10 = 0.20 m, so the difference in pressure is 0.20 × 1000 × 9.8 = 1960 Pa. This is what produces the upthrust.

mcqs.q: A solid block of density 700 kg/m³ is lowered into water of density 1000 kg/m³ and released. What happens to the block?
options: It floats with part of it below the surface of the water.
It floats with all of it above the surface of the water.
It sinks, because a solid block is heavier than water.
It sinks, because 700 kg/m³ is a high density for a solid.
mcqs.explain: The block is less dense than the water, so it comes to rest partially submerged with the upthrust equal to its weight.
